cards.explanation: The answer is Egypt. Verse 3 says, “…and they played in Egypt, prostituting themselves from their youth.” Verse 8 then says Oholah never gave up what she began there. Egypt is where the trouble starts in this picture, friends.

The answer is Jerusalem. God says it plainly in verse 4: “…Oholibah is Jerusalem.” Judah's kings reigned from there (1 Kings 14:21). So when God talks about the younger sister, He is talking about that city.

The answer is True. Verse 5 says, “Oholah prostituted herself while she was still Mine.” She already belonged to God and still went after other lovers. That is the heart of this whole picture, friends, and it's a heavy one.
The answer is the Assyrians. Verse 5 says Oholah lusted after “…her lovers, the Assyrians…” Verse 6 describes them as governors, commanders and horsemen. God names them straight out.
The word is idols. Verse 7 says, “She defiled herself with all the idols of those for whom she lusted.” God ties the Assyrians to their idols. That's a big part of what is going on here.

The answer is True. Verse 9 says, “Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, the Assyrians for whom she lusted.” The ones she chased became the ones who ended up with her. It's a hard verse, friends, and I won't pretend otherwise.
The answer is False. Verse 10 says her lovers “…seized her sons and daughters, and put her to the sword.” Seized, not protected. It's a heavy verse, so let's all take a breath here, friends.

The answer is that she becomes even more depraved. Verse 11 says Oholibah saw what happened to Oholah, “…yet in her lust and prostitution she was more depraved than her sister.” She saw all of it, and it didn't turn her around. That's the sobering part.
The answer is True. Verse 12 says, “She too lusted after the Assyrians…” The details match too: governors, commanders and horsemen. Verse 13 sums it up: “both of them had taken the same path.”

The answer is the Babylonians. Verse 15 says the men on the wall “…looked like officers of the Babylonians in Chaldea, the land of their birth.” She saw them engraved on a wall in vermilion. Chaldea is the land the Babylonians come from.

The word is messengers, friends. Verse 16 says, “At the sight of them, she lusted for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.” She saw pictures on a wall and sent word across the distance. It all started with what she saw.

The answer is that she turns away in disgust. Verse 17 says that after the Babylonians defiled her, “…she turned away in disgust.” The Babylonians came to her, and afterward she was the one who turned away from them. Disgust is the word the text uses.

The answer is True. In verse 18 God says, “…I turned away from her in disgust, just as I had turned away from her sister.” That comes right after she openly prostitutes herself and exposes her nakedness. Both sisters ended up in the same place with Him.
The answer is False. Verse 19 says, “Yet she multiplied her promiscuity, remembering the days of her youth…” She remembers, and she multiplies. Nothing in the verse says she turns back.
The answer is False. In verse 22 God says, “…I will bring them against you from every side…” That means all around her, not one direction.

The answer is their own standards. Verse 24 says, “I will delegate judgment to them, and they will punish you according to their own standards.” God hands the judgment over, and they carry it out by their own measure.
The answer is True. Verse 25 says, “They will seize your sons and daughters…” Verse 10 says the same thing happened to Oholah. The sisters share this heavy fate.

The answer is her indecency and prostitution. Verse 27 says, “So I will put an end to your indecency and prostitution, which began in the land of Egypt…” It began in Egypt and God says it ends here. She will not “…lift your eyes to them or remember Egypt anymore.”

The answer is chasing the nations and their idols. Verse 30 says, “…because you have prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.” Verses 29 and 30 together say her indecency and promiscuity brought these things on her. God spells out the reason Himself, so we don't have to guess.

The answer is that she followed her sister's path. Verse 31 says, “Because you have followed the path of your sister, I will put her cup into your hand.” Same path, same cup. God gives the reason in the same sentence.
The answer is True. Verse 34 says, “You will drink it and drain it…” The cup is deep and wide, and she will drain it to the bottom. It's a heavy word, friends.

The answer is that she forgot Him and pushed Him aside. Verse 35 says, “Because you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your indecency and prostitution.” God puts it in His own words. Two phrases carry it: forgotten Me, and cast Me behind your back.
